title: The Serpent-Charmer and His Wife

full_text:
In a village near Aleppo lived an ambitious snake-charmer named Mansur who caught wild serpents in the rocky hills to perform tricks in the market square. One afternoon, he captured an enormous, venomous black cobra of terrifying power and brought it home in a wicker basket, boasting to his wife:

'Rejoice, wife! With this monstrous serpent, I shall amaze the crowds in the central square and earn fifty silver dirhams every day!'

His prudent wife pleaded with him: 'O husband, be content with harmless grass-snakes! He who harbors a viper beneath his roof invites disaster for a few pieces of silver. Release the beast into the rocky wilderness!'

Mansur laughed scornfully at her fears, placed the wicker basket in the corner of their kitchen, and went to the tavern to celebrate his capture.

While he was absent, the snake rubbed against the wicker lid, worked the latch loose, and crawled onto the floor. When Mansur’s wife entered to prepare the evening meal, she saw the cobra coiled beside the flour-jar, its hood flared and hissing venomously!

Keeping her presence of mind, the courageous woman did not scream. She seized a heavy iron cooking cauldron, dropped it squarely over the serpent, and placed three heavy millstones upon the lid!

When Mansur returned singing and boastful, his wife pointed to the cauldron and handed him his walking staff: 'Pick up your basket and take that monster far into the uninhabited mountains, or seek another hearth! A home is a sanctuary for children, not a cage for venom.'

Mansur blushed with profound shame, released the snake into the distant desert, and resolved never again to risk his family’s safety for reckless gain.
moral: He who brings venomous hazards into his home out of reckless pride endangers those he loves.
